item.title: Background Detection, Blur, and Removal
item.description: Replacing a background sounds like one operation, but it is a pipeline of different problems. A system must decide what the foreground is, estimate how strongly each pixel belongs to it, apply an effect, and composite the result. The best algorithm therefore depends less on a leaderboard than on the input, the amount of user guidance, the hardware, and whether the output is a photograph or an unending live stream.

item.title: Object Detection Algorithms
item.description: Object detection answers two questions: what objects are present, and where are they? A detector normally returns a set of class labels, confidence scores, and bounding boxes. Over several decades, the field has moved from hand-built templates scanned across an image to neural networks that predict many objects in one pass, and then to transformers and vision-language models that can search for categories described in text.

item.title: HTTP Video Streaming
item.description: HTTP video delivery ranges from one seekable file to an adaptive sequence of short media segments. HTTP moves representations and validators; a container organizes timed tracks, and codecs encode the audio and video samples. Keeping those layers separate makes range handling, caching, and playback failures easier to diagnose.

item.title: FFmpeg User Guide
item.description: ffmpeg is a media pipeline tool. It reads one or more inputs, optionally filters the decoded frames, and writes one or more outputs.
